chunks: Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Isa from Muhammad ibn Abi Umayr from Hammad from Muhammad ibn Muslim said:

I asked Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) about the mute person: how does he swear an oath if a debt is claimed against him and the claimant has no proof? He said: 'The Commander of the Faithful (peace be upon him) was brought a mute person, and a debt was claimed against him. He denied it, and the claimant had no proof. The Commander of the Faithful (peace be upon him) said: "Praise be to God who did not take me out of this world until I clarified for the community everything they need."'

Then he said: 'Bring me a Mushaf (copy of the Quran).' It was brought to him, and he said to the mute person: 'What is this?' He raised his head to the sky and indicated that it is the Book of Allah, the Exalted and Mighty.
Then he said: 'Bring me his guardian/wali.' A brother of his was brought, and he seated him beside him. Then he said: 'O Qanbar, bring me an inkwell and a writing tablet.' They were brought to him.
Then he said to the brother of the mute person: 'Tell your brother: this is between you and him.' So he presented it to him with that.
Then the Commander of the Faithful (peace be upon him) wrote: 'By the God who is no god but He, the Knower of the unseen and the witnessed... The Merciful, the Compassionate.'

The Seeker, the Dominant, the Bestower of Harm, the Bestower of Benefit, the Destroyer, the Inevitable, the One who knows the secret and the open. So-and-so ibn so-and-so, the claimant, has no right or claim against so-and-so, meaning the mute person, in any manner or by any reason.
Then he washed the ink (from the tablet) and ordered the mute person to drink it. He refused, so he bound him with the debt.

key_terms.الطَّالِبُ الْغَالِبُ: The Seeker, the Dominant (Divine attributes in the declaration)
key_terms.غَسَلَهُ: He washed it (the ink to be drunk)

ai.seo_question: How did Imam Ali rule on debt claims against a mute person without proof?
ai.summary: This hadith from *Tahdhib al-Ahkam* illustrates Imam Ali’s (AS) judicial innovation in adapting the oath-taking ritual for the mute, utilizing his brother as a scribe to record a formal denial of debt. The subsequent act of drinking the written declaration (*shurb al-kitab*) served as a binding evidentiary seal, reflecting the Shia emphasis on flexible legal mechanisms (*usul*) that address specific physical disabilities while maintaining the integrity of *bayyinah* (proof).
